synthesis: The governance debate has moved past "whether to regulate" and into a contested fight over which institution holds the pen. Responsible-AI advocates are front-loading NDAA pressure ahead of the June 8 SASC markup; OpenAI is explicitly contesting NSA oversight in favor of civilian scientific authority; and CDT is handing state legislators the chatbot-harm taxonomy that 78 live bills have been drafting without. The institutional architecture of U.S. frontier AI governance may be decided in the next 30 days.

items.org: ARI / Alliance for Secure AI / AI Policy Network
items.headline: Three responsible-AI advocacy groups deliver joint letter to Armed Services Committees on NDAA guardrails
items.takeaway: With SASC markup four days out, the coalition is converting VP Vance's "life-and-death decisions in human hands" rhetoric into floor pressure — potentially giving the AI Guardrails Act unexpected bipartisan cover before positions harden.

items.headline: "Dark Patterns in AI Chatbots" catalogs 37 deceptive design patterns across major chatbots
items.takeaway: Seventy-eight chatbot bills are alive in 27 states; CDT's taxonomy hands the state legislative surge the structured harm framework it has been missing.

items.headline: "Democratic Governance of Frontier AI" blueprint rejects NSA-led oversight in favor of CAISI civilian evaluations
items.takeaway: The most visible institutional fault line between a frontier lab and the executive branch in 2026 — whether civilian scientific authority or national-security bodies hold the evaluation keys will define the legitimacy of any federal framework.

items.headline: Project Glasswing expands to 150 critical-infrastructure orgs in 15+ countries; 10,000+ high-severity vulnerabilities found
items.takeaway: The stated 6–12 month window before rival labs ship Mythos-class models without equivalent safeguards is the operational clock driving this expansion.

items.headline: "Cybersecurity's AI Paradox" — criminal AI tools now enabling bank-account draining at industrial scale
items.takeaway: AI is simultaneously the most scalable defense and the most accessible offense — and the offense is deployed ahead of any regulatory framework governing it.

items.headline: "What If AI Retraining Is Just a Comforting Lie?"
items.takeaway: ADP May's 9,000 losses concentrated in AI-exposed information sectors is the empirical backdrop — if the policy response is the manufacturing playbook, midterm-year fallout arrives faster than any program can execute.

items.headline: Japan's AI transition faces structural stumbling blocks despite productivity promise
items.takeaway: Tokyo is simultaneously buying into the allied AI race and unable to force the domestic industrial restructuring that would let it benefit.
